verdict: Yes: merge commit 3d61c548d9b172e03809efd212e3b79a2f129f41 (their commit 7953d4a9d plus one commit of mine), not their commit alone. In the four rules themselves I found no changed optimum and no infeasible postsolve: 122 million release and 47 million assertion campaign models with my own seeds, 60,000 tiny models applied by hand in exact rational arithmetic, and 100,000 tiny models through the engine judged in exact arithmetic are clean. I found and repaired four defects of the milestone, each with a test that failed first: (1) a broken fixed-point contract of the forcing column (R4), (2) an assertion on a cost that underflows in the free singleton column (R2, R5), (3) the family stopping on its budget with nothing to do, which broke identity with the base engine when its reductions are switched off, (4) the integral side and the drift guard of an integer column each using the tolerance on their own, which left a row off by 1.08e-6 at an exactly feasible reduced point. One wrong result is NOT repaired and the owner must know it before the gate: a row removed as a parallel row of 2^18 times the scale of its kept row is violated by 1.56e-3 after the zero-cost singleton rule (R3) rounds a side of the kept row. I do not hold the milestone for it because the base commit 74350acb3 produces the same 1.56e-3 with Stage 1 rules only (parallel rows, then a doubleton substitution); the cause is that the parallel rows keep the row with the smaller index whatever its scale, and it cannot be closed from inside the singleton-column rules. What I did not do: check/structure_check.hpp (1,608 changed lines) was read in its contract and constants and attacked through wrong engines, hand-made results and cost variants, not line by line; nothing ran with a solver; nothing ran on the node.
wrong_results: REPAIRED. Broken fixed-point contract of the forcing column (R4). Input: min y + 2z; row 0: k + y + f <= 1e9 + 4 with k free and without cost, f with bounds [1e9, 1e9]; y + z >= 3; y - z <= 2; y, z integer in [0, 10]. The commit under review returned fixed_point = true with 3 rows and 3 columns, and the presolve of that reduced model then removed k with row 0 (2 rows, 2 columns). Cause: the author added a guard to R4 (the column is left when a side of one of its rows is not readable); a side changes without an event of the column (here when the term of the fixed column leaves the row), and the family tests R4 only for listed columns. Repair in src/rules_singleton_cols.cpp: such a row is marked and lists its live columns when it is listed itself. Tests columns_review_forcing_column_follows_the_sides_of_its_rows and columns_review_fixed_point_with_a_side_that_becomes_readable in tests/test_columns_review.cpp. The campaign cannot reach this (no generated side is beyond 1e8).

REPAIRED. Cost that underflows in the free singleton column (R2, R5). Input: 4k + 2y + 3z = 6 with k free and cost 4.9e-324 (also with the row as an inequality). cost / a is 0, so the code skipped set_cost(k, 0) and removed the column with its cost: assertion 'csc.size[col] == 0 && cost[col] == 0.' in remove_col in the assertion build, a silently dropped cost in the release build. Repair: the column is left when cost / a is zero for a cost that is not. Test columns_review_cost_that_underflows.

REPAIRED. The family with none of its reductions active (all four switched off, or primal-only mode with the free singleton column off) still charged a visit per listed column and could stop on its budget, which clears the fixed-point flag. Against the base engine in the same options the fixed-point flag differed in 986 of 2,160 chunks of 1,000 random models (four reductions off) and in all 2,160 chunks (primal-only without the free singleton column), in each build; reduced models and stacks were equal. Repair: the family then takes its lists and returns, as an unbuilt family does. After it 0 of 2,160,000 models per build differ in each of the two modes. Test columns_review_family_without_an_active_reduction.

REPAIRED. Tolerance used twice where a row gives an integer column its value (R2, R5 for an integer column, and the alias forest). Input: 1000 k + (1000 - 9e-10) y = 1000 + 9.9e-7, k an integer free singleton column, y integer in [0, 100]. The side passed as integral within the feasibility tolerance (9.9e-7) and the drift within its share (9e-8); the column was substituted as k = 1 - y, and the reduced point y = 100, feasible exactly, postsolved to a point that misses the row by 1.08e-6 against the tolerance 1e-6 (scratch probe/stack_tol.cpp). This follows the binding design text (F.2), so it is a design defect that the code inherited. Repair in src/integral.hpp: drift_within also asks side error + |a| * drift <= tol.feasibility. Tests columns_review_integral_side_and_drift_share_the_tolerance and a case in alias_integer_edge_needs_integral_scale_and_offset. Identity with the base and with the commit under review holds on every set I ran, so it refuses nothing there.

NOT REPAIRED. Zero-cost singleton rule (R3) next to a parallel row of larger scale. Input (scratch probe/parallel_scale.cpp, only parallel rows and the singleton family on): r0: s + y + z in [0.1, 5.3]; r1 = 262144 * r0; s continuous in [0, 9e7] without cost; y in [-1e8, 10], z in [0, 1]; two rows keep y and z. The parallel rows remove r1 into r0, R3 then removes s and sets the lower side of r0 to the double -89999999.900000006 (the exact value is -89999999.9). The reduced point y = -89999999.900000006, z = 0 has violation 0 in the reduced model; its postsolve gives s = 9e7 and row r1 is violated by 1.563e-3. The base commit 74350acb3 gives the same 1.563e-3 without any column rule (scratch probe/parallel_scale_base.cpp: r0: y + z in [0.1, 5.3], r1 = 262144 * r0, y - v = 9e7; parallel rows, then the doubleton substitution shifts the sides of r0 by 9e7). With the larger row first (kept) R3 leaves s and nothing is wrong (probe/parallel_scale_swapped.cpp). The cause is in Stage 1: the parallel rows keep the row with the smaller index whatever the scales, so whatever is later written into the kept row at double precision reaches the removed row times the ratio. On probe/parallel_scale.cpp itself the base engine is right and the milestone is wrong; the class is the base's. A guard inside R3 cannot close it, because the undo arithmetic at values of 9e7 has the same rounding. The author listed this as unsure without a model.
other_defects: Statement in their report that is wrong: 'the alias forest repair changes nothing because no built rule uses the forest yet'. The doubleton equations use the forest. The measured part of the claim holds: no result changes on the 17 dumps, the 240 dumps and 4.32 million random models per build.

Their test of the side less the fixed terms (columns_singleton_side_less_the_fixed_terms) uses a column without bounds, so it did not test review item 9 a (fixed terms must enter the implied range once). The code is right; a wrong engine that takes the fixed terms off twice passed all 462 of their tests and is caught only by the campaign. Test added (columns_review_fixed_terms_enter_the_range_once).

No unit test had a row without a finite side before the rows of a forcing column: the wrong engine fc_shift (coefficients of the record not moved up) passed test_columns_singleton.cpp and was caught only by two end-to-end tests and 9 campaign models. Test added.

In campaigns of 1.44 million models, 21 results of the wrong engine zs_room and 35 of fc_first_row failed the oracle with an infeasible postsolved point and passed the structure check. On the 240 dumps without stored points the structure check is the only test of these undos.

Weak check on real instances: the check tool without a solver on the 17 local dumps (both modes, 2 cost variants, 4 pushed points) passes every verdict for 5 of the 8 wrong engines I tried there (fs_fixed, fs_ahead, fs_any_side, zs_infinite, zs_room). Three are caught: fs_not_dual (crush objective and cost variants on brazil3), zs_one_side (unitcal_7), fc_first_row (cost variants on 4 instances).

Blind spots of the campaign generator: 9 of the 99 wrong engines are caught by unit tests only and by no campaign check (1.44 million models each): fs_guard, zs_guard, fc_guard (guards on sides next to fixed terms), fs_drift, r_alias_drift, fs_shared (ratios that are integers only within the tolerance), fs_limited (growth chain), ev_sides (the repair above), ev_scale. No generated model has a side beyond 1e8, a fixed term that swallows a side beside a column of these rules, a ratio off an integer by less than 1e-9, or a chain of pivot ratios above 1000.

ev_unread and ev_scale, as asked: ev_unread is caught by the second presolve of the campaign on 2 of 1,440,000 models with the final sources (1 with the sources of the commit under review: profile equations, seed 9300036821, --columns) and fails 9 unit tests. ev_scale is caught by no campaign check and fails 5 unit tests; the singleton family reads nothing that only a column event of scale_row would bring.

Clause 5 of the crush check is generous: on the review model of item 4 a record with the pivot coefficient 0.5 or -1 instead of 1 still passes the round trip and the row test (the allowance is computed with the record's own coefficient, and the row violation of 1e-4 is below the relative tolerance). The author names this in part.

The oracle compares objectives relative to the value: with costs scaled by 2^30 or 2^50 it gives 655 alarms on 1,200,000 models of the profile --columns, 452 with the base engine on the same models. All are of that kind or 'outside the oracle class'. The cost that R2 and R5 move adds rounding of the cost terms. The structure check fails on none of the 645,070 results there.

push_forcing_col with no saved row is guarded by an assertion only: a wrong engine that takes the infinite side of every row (v_r4_mirror in my scratch) crashes the release build with a segmentation fault instead of failing a check.

Not this milestone's, reported as asked: (a) profile huge_parallel, seed 10100538218, variant 8, no profile option, assertion campaign: 'the reduced optimum is 0.99999999889066382, the base optimum 1'. It is the known 1.1e-9 class; the base engine fails it identically in both builds, also with the family off, and the family has no finding. assumptions.title: Rows marked for the forcing column (mine)
assumptions.statement: When the forcing column (R4) is left because a side of one of its rows, or that side less the fixed terms, is not readable, the row is marked. A marked row that is listed puts all its live columns on the column list, at the cost of one scan of the row, and loses the mark.
assumptions.alternatives: Report limited when the guard refuses a column; test the columns of every listed row; drop the guard (not valid).
assumptions.measured: 17 and 240 local dumps: results identical to the commit under review, so no mark changed a result there. Campaign: not reachable by the generator.

assumptions.title: Family without an active reduction (mine)
assumptions.statement: When none of the four reductions is active the call takes both lists and returns without work, so it cannot stop on its budget.
assumptions.switch: no switch (follows options_t::sub_enabled and options_t::primal_only through sub_rule_active)
assumptions.alternatives: Charge a visit per listed column as before.
assumptions.measured: Random models, per build: before, 986 of 2,160 chunks of 1,000 models differ from the base engine with the four reductions off and 2,160 of 2,160 in primal-only mode without the free singleton column (fixed-point flag only); after, 0 of 2,160,000 models in each mode.

assumptions.title: A cost that cannot be moved leaves the column (partly mine)
assumptions.statement: The free singleton column (R2, R5) is left when cost / a is not finite, when it is zero for a cost that is not (mine), when its product with the side is not finite, or when a new cost of another column would not be finite. Their report names none of these among the assumptions.
assumptions.alternatives: Drop a cost that underflows; clamp.
assumptions.measured: not measured (no dump or generated model has such a cost)

assumptions.title: Integral side and drift share the feasibility tolerance (mine)
assumptions.statement: Where a row gives an integer column its value, |a * m - side| plus |a| times the drift must stay within tol.feasibility, on top of the drift's own share. Applies to R2 and R5 for an integer column and to an edge of the alias forest between integer columns. A drift share above 1 therefore no longer admits more than the tolerance.
assumptions.switch: tolerances_t::integral_drift_share = 0.1 and tolerances_t::feasibility = 1e-6 (no switch for the sum)
assumptions.alternatives: Each within its own limit, as the design text F.2 has it (up to 1.1 tolerances in a row).
assumptions.measured: Model 1000 k + (1000 - 9e-10) y = 1000 + 9.9e-7: 1.08e-6 before, refused after. 17 and 240 local dumps and 4,320,000 random models per build: no result changes.

assumptions.title: A row is an equation only when its sides are equal exactly
assumptions.statement: The visit takes the free singleton column of an equation (R2, primal) when row_lower == row_upper as doubles; a row whose sides differ in the last bit is treated as an inequality (R5 needs a cost and is off in primal-only mode) or by the zero-cost rule.

assumptions.title: Place of the family in the round
assumptions.statement: The family is called once per round, after the cascade, the parallel rows, the doubleton equations and simple probing, and before the dual and parallel column families. A doubleton equation with a singleton column is therefore the doubleton rule's, and the parallel rows read singleton columns before this family removes them.
assumptions.alternatives: Before the parallel rows; inside the cascade.

assumptions.title: Band of the implied-bound test, its constants
assumptions.statement: The band is 2 * (4 rounding units * |bound| + activity_error_share * feasibility), about 2e-7 for small bounds; the factor 2 and the 4 rounding units are bare constants of the groundwork. Their list names only the two tolerances.
assumptions.switch: tolerances_t::activity_error_share = 0.1 and tolerances_t::feasibility; no switch for the factor 2 and candidate_rounding_units = 4
assumptions.alternatives: Rounding only (as the design asks of R6); the full feasibility tolerance.
assumptions.measured: A band of 1e-3 (wrong engine fs_band) gives 30 oracle and 34 structure failures in 1,440,000 campaign models. Other widths: not measured.

assumptions.title: New sides of the zero-cost rule that cross
assumptions.statement: When the two new sides of R3 end with lower above upper (two differences equal to the last bit), the visit does nothing.
assumptions.alternatives: Set both sides to one value.

assumptions.title: Work that the family charges
assumptions.statement: 8 units (line_visit_work) per listed live column and row; the used slots of a row per scan, per save and per deletion; for a forcing column its used slots plus twice those of its rows, tested against the rest of the budget before the reduction. These charges decide where a budget stops a call and so which reductions a call makes.
assumptions.switch: options_t::budget[rule::singleton_cols] = {8, 4, 100000} for the limits; no switch for the charges
assumptions.alternatives: Other charges; no pre-check for the forcing column.
assumptions.measured: 17 local dumps: 14,764,231 units for the family, identical before and after my commit.

assumptions.title: A ratio that is not an integer exactly next to a column without a finite bound
assumptions.statement: integral_term gives such a ratio an infinite drift, so the row is never integral for the column, whatever the share is.
assumptions.switch: no switch (any finite tolerances_t::integral_drift_share refuses it)

assumptions.title: Which of two parallel rows is kept (Stage 1, decides the validity of what the column rules write into a row)
assumptions.statement: The parallel rows keep the row with the smaller index whatever the scales of the two. A side or a value that a later rule writes into the kept row at double precision reaches the removed row times the ratio.
assumptions.where: gpu_presolve/include/gprs/rules.hpp, rule (e), 'the one with the smaller index is kept'; gpu_presolve/src/rules_parallel_rows.cpp
assumptions.alternatives: Keep the row of the larger scale; bound the ratio times the size of the terms; carry a reach factor per row that the later rules guard with.
assumptions.measured: Ratio 2^18 with a term of 9e7: 1.563e-3 violation of the removed row through R3 (probe/parallel_scale.cpp) and through a doubleton substitution at the base commit (probe/parallel_scale_base.cpp); with the larger row kept, none.
